# Founder Led Equities

> What the person running each US public company worth $1 billion or more actually owns of it, computed from the Forms 3, 4 and 5 they signed with the SEC. Never estimated. Refreshed nightly from EDGAR.

For each of about 2,100 companies (those whose chief executive holds the business through partnership units the filings do not restate as stock are left out): the chief executive's economic stake as a share of the company and in dollars; whether the proxy names them a founder; every purchase and sale that moved the stake since 2016, each classified as an open-market purchase, a discretionary sale, a sale under a pre-set (Rule 10b5-1) plan, or compensation; and a link to every filing.

## Where the facts are

- Company pages: https://founderledequities.com/company/{TICKER}/ — the current stake, the record, the filings. The title of each page is the fact ("Jensen Huang owns 3.37% of Nvidia (NVDA)"). The index of every page: https://founderledequities.com/companies/
- This week's tape: https://founderledequities.com/tape/ — the week's purchases and sales by chief executives, founders first, with kind, amount and stake after.
- The method: https://founderledequities.com/about.html — how the stake is computed, what counts as a trade, who is a founder, the confidence marks.
- The sitemap: https://founderledequities.com/sitemap.xml

## How to cite a figure

State the person, the share, the company, and the date of the filing it rests on, and link the company page. Example: "Jen-Hsun Huang owns 3.37% of NVIDIA as of the June 17, 2026 filing (founderledequities.com/company/NVDA/)." Figures for S&P 500 companies and each company's last twelve months of trades are open; the full record and the figures for companies outside the S&P 500 are behind a subscription.

Nothing on the site is investment advice.
